document.abstract: The adoption of the ATSC's Digital Television Standard means that pictures may be broadcast in a number of different formats rather than the 525/601 system used for analog NTSC. Many television stations have already declared their proposed formats for standard definition (SD) and high definition (HD), and it is clear that several will soon be in use. This paper establishes aims for such a scheme, examines possible ways of working with multiple input and output formats in post-production, and formulates a practical structure for such equipment. It also looks at the possible impact this may have on operational practices.

authors.bio: Bob Pank is the technical communications manager for Quantel Ltd., U.K. Among his many duties, he contributes papers to technical conferences, pens technical articles, and has edited several books, including the Digital Fact Book . His more recent work has involved the Internet and other new media. After graduating with Honors in electrical engineering from Imperial College, London, Pank gained four years of television experience as a videotape engineer with the British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC). In 1976, he joined Quantel organization, where his job involved engineering support for sales and marketing. This included introducing new products to many countries and the opportunity to witness the spread of digital techniques throughout the television industry. He later became responsible for management of graphics products and was appointed to his current position in 1992. Pank is a member of SMPTE and the Royal Television Society.
